gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-oxygen: Conthrax bends its strokes like a paperclip, and its lowercase a opens its mouth wide. But Oxygen, a plain sans, leaves its curves open and softens the geometric heading beside it.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-preahvihear: Geometric and clean, Conthrax draws every glyph with one-tip simplicity. Preahvihear, a plain sans with mouths open like a pried oyster and a lofty x-height, carries paragraphs with a steady, unhurried flow.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-puritan: Clean fits both: Conthrax has no thin strokes to vanish in glare, while the sans-serif Puritan keeps rounded forms open. Nothing thin, nothing cramped: sturdy legibility runs through both.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-questrial: Modern throughout: Conthrax gives a wide-mouthed lowercase a and tall bodies, while Questrial, a plain sans, keeps its letters open. Its single-weight strokes keep paragraphs moving smoothly, like following one thread.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-radio-canada: Conthrax stretches a wide-mouthed lowercase a across bodies so tall the capitals barely rise above them, in clean, geometric lines. Radio Canada holds a steady line and open curves through each paragraph.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-sarpanch: Approachable Sarpanch sits beneath a heading that never shifts weight. Conthrax is best at wide, tall-bodied geometry, while the sans-serif Sarpanch is best at an open e and compact lines.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-sintony: Clean from the first stroke, Conthrax keeps every line free of contrast. Sintony, a plain sans with a chunky, tall midzone and no clogged curves, keeps the whole pairing reading smoothly.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-sofia-sans: Tall as cut acrylic, Sofia Sans has no stroke modulation at all. Conthrax leads with wide-mouthed geometry up top, and the sans-serif Sofia Sans rounds things off with open sides below.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-aldrich: Glyphs set well apart give Disorder its raw, chaotic scatter, while Aldrich, a sans, keeps lowercase near capital height. Raw above, modern below, and the gap between them is the draw.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-alexandria: Alexandria sets generously open c terminals and a tall body beneath Disorder, whose ink looks poured, with no swelling at the joins. Alexandria, a sans, reads steadily paragraph to paragraph, its short stems keeping lines tidy.
